verification.reason: The failure path holds in the code I read. `mutantLister()` calls `adapter.install()` inside the fulfilment handler of `.then(onOk, onErr)`. `onErr` only handles rejections from `open`, so it cannot catch a throw from `onOk`. `Install.read` → `Walk.#scan` counts every directory it enters, including all the "tree" subdirectories inside each package. It throws `InstalledPackagesError` once `#entered.size >= 50_000`. `mutantLister()` therefore rejects, and `await mutantLister()` at review.ts:2976 has no catch. Any review that selects a lens offering `list_mutants` (the built-in tests lens) aborts for a checkout whose instrumenter install is that large. The base keyed only the instrumenter's version and source, with no install walk, and the same repository reviewed fine. The bound counts every file-tree directory rather than packages, so a large monorepo install can plausibly exceed it. The head decision doc says the bound is meant to fail the review. It also says the unreadable-directory and manifest cases deliberately do not abort, because "a review that reuses nothing is better than one that aborts". The bound case is left out of that reasoning. I did not run a real 50k-directory install, so whether a given customer install exceeds the bound is unverified.
